title: Quantum Fisher Information and the Speed of Entanglement
abstract: We investigate the speed at which entanglement can be generated by an interaction parameter encoded in a two-qubit Hamiltonian, quantified by the derivative of concurrence with respect to the coupling parameter. For arbitrary pure two-qubit states evolving under a general nonlocal interaction, we derive a bound relating this entanglement speed to the quantum Fisher information (QFI). Specifically, we show that $|\partial_g C| \le \sqrt{F_Q^{(g)}}$, where $F_Q^{(g)}$ is the QFI associated with estimation of the parameter. This establishes $\sqrt{F_Q}$ as a an upper bound on the speed of entanglement generation in parameter space. We further derive the saturation conditions and identify the states and dynamical regimes for which equality is attained. At saturation, concurrence evolves at the maximum rate permitted by the distinguishability of the underlying quantum state. These results reveal a direct connection between quantum metrology and entanglement generation, showing that the same information-theoretic quantity that governs parameter-estimation precision also limits the speed at which entanglement resources can be created.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a fundamental upper bound connecting the speed of entanglement generation to the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI). By analyzing two-qubit evolution, it proves that the rate at which entanglement changes cannot exceed a value determined by the QFI. This result unifies concepts from quantum metrology and entanglement dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates establishing a fundamental upper bound on the speed at which entanglement can be generated by varying an interaction parameter in a two-qubit system.
main_result: A direct inequality, $|\partial_g C| \leq \sqrt{	ext{QFI}}$, is derived, showing that the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) limits the rate of change of concurrence with respect to the coupling parameter $g$.
method: The analysis employs rigorous mathematical bounding techniques, including differentiation and applying inequalities like Cauchy–Schwarz, to relate the derivative of entanglement measures to information-theoretic quantities.
model_or_system: The system consists of two interacting qubits governed by a general nonlocal Hamiltonian $H(g) = g h$. The dynamics are analyzed for pure states evolving under this interaction parameterization.
key_observables: Concurrence ($C$), Quantum Fisher Information ($	ext{QFI}$), and the entanglement speed, defined as $|\partial_g C|$.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $g$, which controls the evolution; the QFI itself acts as a limiting scale.
main_assumptions: The derivation is primarily restricted to pure two-qubit states undergoing smooth evolution where concurrence is differentiable.
paper_structure: The paper develops the bound by first defining the entanglement speed via the derivative of concurrence, then relating this derivative to the QFI using mathematical inequalities, and finally characterizing the conditions under which this upper bound is saturated.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, information-theoretic constraint on quantum dynamics, linking resource generation (entanglement) directly to parameter estimation precision (QFI), which is crucial for understanding optimal control in quantum systems.
